title: Moving apartments in 10 days: what happens each day
summary: A day-by-day plan that front-loads the paperwork and leaves only boxes for the final weekend.

blocks.title: Ten days, one apartment to another
blocks.body: The anxiety of a fast move comes from everything feeling simultaneous. It is not. Each day has one job, and the jobs have an order - paper first, stuff last. Here is the order.

items.title: Paper day
items.detail: Give notice if required, sign the new lease, book the freight elevator at both ends, and schedule movers or reserve the truck. Everything else waits on these four.

items.title: Utilities and address
items.detail: Set electric and internet start dates at the new place, end dates at the old one the day AFTER you leave. File the mail forwarding order.

items.title: Supplies and purge
items.detail: Buy more boxes than feels reasonable, tape, markers, bags. Walk every room and fill three trash bags of things that are not coming.

items.title: Storage and decor
items.detail: Pack everything off shelves and walls. Books, decorations, spare linens. Label boxes with room and contents, not just room.

items.title: Closet triage
items.detail: Pack out-of-season and occasion clothes. Leave one week's wardrobe out. Donate the maybe pile today, not on moving day.

items.title: Kitchen, mostly
items.detail: Pack all but one pan, one pot, a plate and a fork per person. Eat the freezer down this week.

items.title: The awkward middle
items.detail: Disassemble what you can: shelving, the desk, the spare bed. Photograph cable setups before unplugging anything.

items.title: Everything but the kit
items.detail: Pack to the walls. What stays out fits in one overnight bag: bedding, toiletries, chargers, two days of clothes, the coffee maker, toilet paper, a box cutter.

items.title: Clean and confirm
items.detail: Clean the old place room by room as it empties. Reconfirm elevator slots and movers by text, in writing.

items.title: Move day
items.detail: Overnight bag and paperwork travel with you, never in the truck. Do the old-place walkthrough with photos before handing over keys.

blocks.heading: The first-night box rides up front

items.label: Bedding and pillows
items.detail: Making the bed is the only unpacking that cannot wait.

items.label: Toiletries and medications
items.detail: Plus a towel. Searching boxes for a toothbrush at midnight is the classic low point.

items.label: Chargers
items.detail: Phone, laptop. Tape them into one bag.

items.label: Toilet paper, soap, light bulbs
items.detail: The three things new apartments never have.

items.label: Box cutter and basic tools
items.detail: You cannot open the boxes without the box cutter. Ask how people learn this.

blocks.title: The two things that actually blow up a move
blocks.body: Elevator reservations and key logistics. Buildings book freight elevators out and cancel unconfirmed slots, and a lease that starts on the 1st does not guarantee keys before noon. Confirm both in writing on day 9. Everything else - a missing box, a scratched dresser - is recoverable.
